messages:
Maya Patel: Hey team — brand new here. Running docker-compose up for the app and the Postgres container keeps re-initializing (losing data) every time I restart compose. Using a host bind mount ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data. Any obvious mistakes?

Alex Kim: welcome! :wave: Mac + bind mounts are a common gotcha. Docker Desktop's file sharing and permission translations can cause initdb to think the dir is empty and reinit. Two quick options: use a named Docker volume or set PGDATA to a subdir. Also check Docker Desktop -> Use gRPC FUSE (toggle helped me).

Maya Patel: Ah ok. I used bind mount because I wanted files on host for debugging. Is named volume still ok for local dev?

Sam Carter: Named volume is usually fine and keeps data persistent across restarts without host fs permission weirdness. Example snippet that works for me: 

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devpass
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

Sam Carter: Note PGDATA points inside container to avoid initdb trying to write to a dir owned by root on mac.

John R.: If you absolutely need host bind mount, chown the host dir to postgres uid (999) and use the PGDATA trick:

```bash
# for host bind mount dir
sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata

# or for a named volume (run once to fix perms)
docker run --rm -v yourproject_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data alpine sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /var/lib/postgresql/data"
```

Lily Nguyen: fyi docker-compose down -v will remove volumes (so backups first). If you try the named-volume route and still see re-init, check for leftover init scripts in ./docker-entrypoint-initdb.d — those will only run on a truly empty data dir.

Maya Patel: @Alex @Sam thanks — I didn't realize PGDATA mattered. I'll try switching to a named volume and running the chown command. Would it be reasonable to keep a host copy for SQL files only?

Alex Kim: Yup, keep SQL or migrations as a separate bind (./migrations:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d) but be careful — those scripts will run on an empty volume only. For iterative dev you can mount psql client scripts but not the whole PGDATA.

Maya Patel: sweet, trying now. I'll report back. Thanks everyone! :heart:
